clue.text: Pudding, not starter, interrupting fish dish

indicators.note: interrupting says the trimmed pudding breaks into the fish word

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: not starter says the first letter of the pudding word is dropped

parts.note: duff is a boiled suet pudding, as in plum duff

explanation.surface: A dessert-free menu where the opening course has somehow got mixed into the fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pudding' looks like the definition, but it is the old suet pudding that loses its first letter; the dish is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light baked egg creation is a classic French dish, savoury or sweet.

clue.text: Club welcoming hot talent

indicators.note: welcoming says the club word takes the hot letter in

parts.note: a stick is a club or cudgel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A nightclub takes on an exciting new act.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's routine or special gimmick, from Yiddish, is their particular talent.

clue.text: State that is dividing America, pants?

definitions.note: plural noun matching the plural answer; pants is British for underpants

indicators.note: dividing says the state and that-is letters split the America letters

parts.note: US is the United States of America
ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota, a US state
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: Asks whether a divisive state is rubbish, 'pants' being British slang for poor.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pants' means underwear (and, as slang, rubbish), which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for underwear, which British English calls pants.

clue.text: With rigging of ballot admitted, suits go to pieces

indicators.note: admitted says the rigged letters are let into the suits word

parts.note: fits means suits, as in 'that fits me'

indicators.note: rigging of an election suggests the ballot letters are fiddled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tale of vote rigging that makes the suited officials crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is only a link; 'rigging of' scrambles the ballot and 'admitted' lets the result into the suits word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for collapsing or disintegrating, physically or emotionally.

clue.text: Five into nine, the rational number

definitions.note: something that numbs, i.e. an anaesthetic

indicators.note: five into says to take five consecutive letters from within the following words

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle about dividing five into nine and getting a rational number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not a figure; the maths surface is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was an early anaesthetic, something that deadens feeling.

clue.text: See 26
Greek dramatist breaks to pocket first of cash, after bribe

indicators.note: after says the breaks part follows the bribe

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

indicators.note: to pocket says the breaks word takes in the cash letter

parts.note: holes are breaks or gaps

indicators.note: first of says to take the opening letter of cash

explanation.surface: A Greek playwright's rest periods are used to pocket bribe money.
explanation.definitionFit: Author of Oedipus Rex, one of the three great Athenian tragedians.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink preferable, not teetotal

indicators.note: not says the teetotal letters are removed

parts.note: better means preferable

explanation.surface: An alcoholic drink is preferable to abstaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewed from malted grain and hops, it is the commonest alcoholic drink in pubs.

clue.text: A philanthropist controlling computers proves perturbing

indicators.note: controlling says the philanthropist's name holds the computers letters within

parts.note: Bill Gates, Microsoft founder and philanthropist
IT is information technology, i.e. computers

explanation.surface: A wealthy donor who runs computers is causing unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The philanthropist is Bill Gates of Microsoft, apt for 'computers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or unsettle is the verb's meaning, so 'proves perturbing' fits.

clue.text: Dangerous Goth losing heart in the clutches of wicked Irish king

indicators.note: in the clutches of says the reduced Goth sits inside the wicked Irish king
wicked suggests the Irish letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: anagram fodder
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: losing heart says the middle letters of the Goth word go

explanation.surface: A Goth, heartbroken, is held by a villainous Irish monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' empties the middle of the Goth; 'wicked' scrambles Irish, giving HIRIS before the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying great chance of harm is dangerous.

clue.text: Forever turning old and dirty, every second lying back

indicators.note: lying back says those letters are read in reverse
every second says to take the second, fourth and so on of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone forever spinning, old and filthy, reclining every other moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of OLD AND DIRTY are L, A, D, I, T; 'lying back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides ebb and flow endlessly, so a tidal thing is always on the turn.

clue.text: On with it!

definitions.meaning: taking place, as in 'the party is on'

explanation.surface: A brisk command to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both taking place now and fashionably lively, matching both senses.

clue.text: English author the Guardian's translated is back on the box

indicators.note: on says the reversed word is placed after the box word

parts.note: a chest is a box

indicators.note: is back says the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: the Guardian speaking of itself says 'our'; into French that is notre

explanation.surface: An English writer, translated by this newspaper, returns to television.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian's = OUR, translated into French = NOTRE, reversed to ERTON. 'the box' looks like television but is a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer, creator of Father Brown.

clue.text: Fishwife who survived?

parts.note: read as fish plus wife who survived: a young salmon, and the sixth wife of Henry VIII, who outlived him

explanation.surface: A fishmonger woman who lived through something.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Fishwife': the word is a young salmon, and Catherine of that surname was the wife who survived Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a young salmon and the surname of the queen who outlived Henry VIII.

clue.text: Venial story about Pasquale, perhaps?

indicators.note: about says the story word goes round the Pasquale word

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
Don Pasquale is a Donizetti opera, so Pasquale is one example of a Don

explanation.surface: A forgivable little tale about a man named Pasquale.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a minor, excusable one, so forgivable.

clue.text: In basic parts of music, end improvised around heavy metal for maestri

definitions.note: plural noun matching the plural answer

indicators.note: in says what follows is placed within the music parts

parts.note: bars are the basic units into which music is divided

indicators.note: around says the improvised letters go round the metal
improvised says the end letters are rearranged on the spot

parts.note: anagram fodder
lead is a heavy metal

explanation.surface: Conductors improvising a heavy metal ending to basic music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' rearranges 'end' to NDE, and 'around' wraps it round the metal; 'In' places all that within the music parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri are distinguished conductors, and those leading dance bands fit that role.

clue.text: Blinking Titanic sunk, no good

indicators.note: sunk suggests the Titanic letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The Titanic has gone down, no good at all, with 'Blinking' as a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is to wink or blink, a zoological term.

clue.text: Delicate creature, speaking clock needs to rest voice?

indicators.note: speaking says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: clock means see (slang, 'did you clock that?') and needing to rest the voice means hoarse

explanation.surface: A fragile being, with a talking clock that has lost its voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is slang for notice, i.e. see; 'speaking clock' is a decoy for the telephone time service.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fragile marine fish with a horse-like head is a delicate creature.

clue.text: Some fortification in fleece and horns, for example?

definitions.meaning: defensive walls or embankments around a fort

explanation.surface: Fortifications built of wool and horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Defensive embankments are fortifications; split, the word gives pieces of a male sheep.

clue.text: Deals with cities built to be stretched?

indicators.note: built suggests the letters are put together into a new structure

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Property deals involving cities built so large they become overstretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Made elastic, so able to stretch, like a waistband.

clue.text: Capital cheers outstanding nation

indicators.note: outstanding read as standing outside: the cheers letters stand outside the nation

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
Iran is a nation

explanation.surface: A toast to a nation that excels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Cock and hen?

definitions.meaning: a hen pecks, so is one that pecks

explanation.surface: Male and female chickens paired together.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang word for the male member, and literally a bird that jabs with its beak.

clue.text: Bound to need patience, ultimately — a virtue?

parts.note: to hop is to bound or spring

indicators.note: ultimately says to take the final letter of patience

explanation.surface: Patience, in the end, must be a virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like the virtue in the proverb, but it only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three theological virtues, with faith and charity.

clue.text: Dressing prime minister, one is an oddball

parts.note: Theresa May, UK prime minister 2016 to 2019

indicators.note: oddball suggests the following letters are behaving strangely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A prime minister getting dressed is called an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was Britain's prime minister when this ran.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-and-oil sauce is a salad dressing.

clue.text: Trump gone, party!

parts.note: out means gone, as in 'he's out'
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Celebrating that the US president has left office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' is a verb here, to beat, not the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump someone is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Drink a can, almost

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: can and stir are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: Nearly a whole can of something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for prison, as is STIR, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so a drink.

clue.text: Short garment beginning to rise in sketch by a couple of artists

indicators.note: a couple of says the artists abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in says the rise letter goes inside the sketch

parts.note: a skit is a comic sketch

indicators.note: beginning to says to take the first letter of rise

explanation.surface: A hemline rises in a drawing by two painters.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pleated skirt as worn by cheerleaders is a brief garment.

clue.text: Old group ending in tub can't get c-clean?

indicators.note: ending in says to take the final letter of tub

parts.note: lacks means can't get, is without
a clean is a bath; the stutter on c-clean asks for a stammered a b-bath

explanation.surface: A tub that ends up unable to get properly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'c-clean' signals a stammered version, a b-bath, giving the double B.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneering heavy metal band formed in Birmingham in 1968.

clue.text: Gain in knots with set distance travelled

indicators.note: in knots suggests the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Making headway at sea measured in knots over a set distance.
explanation.definitionFit: In navigation, the distance a ship travels eastward is its easting.

clue.text: Outside broadcast on golf tournament

indicators.note: on says the broadcast word follows the tournament word

parts.note: the Open is a famous golf championship
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A TV outside broadcast covering a golf event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is Britain's major golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking place outdoors rather than indoors means outside.
